status_summary: No enacted law defining the location of a telehealth service as the provider's location was found. H.R. 5357, the College Students Continuation of Mental Health Care Act of 2025, introduced 2025-09-15, would let college mental health providers licensed in their institution's state serve students by telehealth wherever the students are located, with scope of practice and malpractice coverage tied to the provider's primary state; it is narrower than the general definition the Mandate seeks. HRSA's Licensure Portability Grant Program page lists awards to licensing-board organizations that predate this period, and a broad Medicare telehealth bill, S. 1261, addresses payment location rules rather than licensure. The GovInfo bill status records show no action on H.R. 5357 after its 2025-09-15 referral (it had 19 cosponsors by 2026-07-13) and none on S. 1261 after its 2025-04-02 referral to Finance.

timeline.event: H.R. 5357 was introduced and referred to the Energy and Commerce and Education and Workforce committees; it would let college mental health providers furnish telehealth to students in other states under the license and scope of practice of the provider's primary state.

title: Define the legal location of a telehealth service as the provider's location
uncertainties: Bill status for H.R. 5357 and S. 1261 was read on GovInfo (latest actions 2025-09-15 and 2025-04-02, referrals only). The HRSA program page carries a July 2024 review date and describes awards that predate this period. The industry tracker was used only as a lead for bill titles and is not proof of absence. Telehealth flexibilities extended in appropriations laws concern Medicare payment, not this definition. Other licensure portability bills may exist that were not found; no full search of all bills was run, and one web search on 2026-10-18 for a general provider-location licensure bill returned only bills from earlier Congresses and state measures. The S. 1261 bill status was read by the researcher and not re-opened.
